items.q: Two CAN nodes start transmitting at the same instant, one with ID 0x120 and one with ID 0x0A5. Which message goes through first?
options: Both are destroyed and an error frame is sent
Whichever node has the faster crystal
items.explain: Dominant 0 bits win arbitration, so the numerically lower ID always gets the bus first.

items.q: A CAN bus runs at 500 kbit/s with 16 time quanta per bit. What is the length of one time quantum?
items.explain: One bit lasts 1 / 500 kHz = 2 µs, and 2 µs / 16 = 125 ns per quantum.

items.q: Bit timing is set as Sync = 1, Prop = 5, Phase1 = 6, Phase2 = 4 time quanta. Where is the sample point?
items.explain: The bit is sampled at the end of Phase1, which is (1 + 5 + 6) / 16 = 12 / 16 = 75% of the bit time.

items.q: In a standard CAN 2.0A data frame, what does the DLC field tell the receiver?
items.explain: DLC is the Data Length Code, 4 bits that say how many data bytes follow.

items.q: With the ECUs powered off, you measure 120 Ω between CAN_H and CAN_L. What does this tell you?
options: One of the two 120 Ω terminators is missing
items.explain: A healthy bus has two 120 Ω terminators in parallel, so the meter should read about 60 Ω.

items.q: A node's transmit error counter climbs to 130. What state is the node in now?
items.explain: A counter above 127 makes the node error passive; it goes bus off only when the transmit error counter passes 255.

items.q: During arbitration a node transmits a recessive bit but reads a dominant bit back from the bus. What does it do?
options: Retries in the very next bit slot
Continues, because the bits are ORed anyway
Stops transmitting and switches to receiving
items.explain: Reading dominant while sending recessive means another node with a higher-priority ID is on the bus, so the node backs off and retries after that frame.

items.q: A CAN transmitter sends the bit pattern 0000000 (seven zeros) in the data field. How many bits actually appear on the wire for these seven?
items.explain: After five identical bits the transmitter inserts one opposite stuff bit, so seven zeros become 00000 1 00 = 8 bits.

items.q: In a LIN cluster, which node sends the header (break, sync, protected ID) for every frame?
options: The node with the lowest ID
items.explain: LIN is single-master: only the master schedules and starts frames, slaves just fill the response when their ID is called.

items.q: The LIN sync field is always 0x55. Why that value?
options: It tells the slave which checksum to use
It carries the LIN protocol version
Its 0101 0101 pattern lets slaves measure the master's bit rate
It is the master's node address
items.explain: 0x55 gives evenly spaced edges, so a slave with a cheap RC oscillator can time them and lock to the master's baud rate.

items.q: A standard 8-byte CAN frame is about 111 bits (ignoring stuffing). One ECU sends such a frame every 10 ms on a 500 kbit/s bus. Roughly what bus load does that message alone add?
items.explain: 111 bits at 2 µs per bit take 222 µs, and 222 µs out of every 10 ms is 2.2%.
